solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Urban trade debt ruined livelihood

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and knocked out of shape, so these three words' letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A city business is sunk by its debts, and someone loses their living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' tells you to rearrange all the letters of URBAN TRADE DEBT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase means the basic earnings a person lives on, their everyday living.

clue.text: Infant suit in reserve in pouch with bits of rusk and ointment

indicators.note: the second 'in' puts the reserve piece inside the pouch piece

parts.note: a pouch is a bag
something put by is kept in reserve, so 'by' means in reserve

indicators.note: bits of here means just the first letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A list of baby things: something kept in reserve in a bag, along with rusks and ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In reserve' is BY in the sense of 'put by'; the second 'in' puts it inside the pouch, and 'bits of' picks first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name now used generally for a baby's all-in-one stretch garment, so an outfit worn by an infant.

clue.text: In year international green effect could become this economical

indicators.note: the words could become something else once their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Talk of green effects in an international year turning things thrifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' rearranges IN, Y, I, GREEN and EFFECT; 'this' just points to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with low power consumption is thrifty with fuel, so economical in its running.

clue.text: Welshman's raised floor

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, the Welsh short form of David
the possessive 's supplies the S

explanation.surface: Describes a Welsh man's stage or platform.
explanation.walkthrough: DAI is the stock Welshman of crosswords; read 'Welshman's' as DAI plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a low platform at the end of a hall, a stage raised above the rest of the room.

clue.text: Cutting top from joint unfortunately led to injection

indicators.note: cutting the top from a word means removing its first letter

parts.note: the knee is a joint

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters of 'led' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Knee surgery has gone badly and the patient ended up needing a jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting top from' takes K off KNEE to leave NEE; 'unfortunately' rearranges LED into DLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the hypodermic and the jab it gives are the same thing, so a shot can be called by the syringe's sharp part.

clue.text: Vile folk finally caught in lowest storey

parts.note: base means low and vile
men means people or folk

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word caught

explanation.surface: Wicked people were at last captured in the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom level of a building, usually below ground, is its cellar storey.

clue.text: Instrument playing at number 10

indicators.note: playing, as in playing about, has the letters moved around

parts.note: the number 10 is written as the figures 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Someone is playing a musical instrument at house number 10.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges AT, NUMBER and IO, where 10 is read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand drum with jingling metal discs, an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Unwinding, relax with rural city cure, not Ely sadly, in sort of activity outside normal routine

definitions.text: sort of activity outside normal routine
definitions.note: describes the adjective as it applies to activities beyond the timetable

indicators.note: unwinding a coil loosens and reorders it, signalling a rearrangement of the fodder
not tells you some letters are missing from the rearranged pool
sadly, things gone wrong, confirms the mixing that leaves out those letters

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds with a country cure for the city, but sadly not in the cathedral city of Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of RELAX, RURAL, CITY and CURE, with the letters of ELY taken away, rearrange to the answer. 'Unwinding' and 'sadly' signal the rearrangement and 'not' the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally beyond the school curriculum, so describing pursuits done outside the usual timetable.

clue.text: Kills last of dipterous insects

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the word dipterous

parts.note: mites are tiny bugs, loosely called insects here

explanation.surface: Something deadly to the last of the two-winged flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dipterous' means two-winged, like flies; strictly mites are arachnids, but the clue loosely calls them insects.
explanation.definitionFit: To smite is to strike hard, and in older usage to strike dead, so it means slays.

clue.text: Most direct route made by black fish in middle of ocean

parts.note: B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black
an eel is a fish
taken as written

indicators.note: middle of picks the centre letter of the word ocean

explanation.surface: A dark fish swims the shortest route through the mid-ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the straightest path, from the way bees supposedly fly directly back to the hive.

clue.text: End of May marks beginning of pandemic in most unusual sign of disease

indicators.note: in puts the gathered letters inside the rearranged word
unusual signals the letters of most arranged in an unusual way
end of takes the final letter of May

parts.note: M is short for marks, the old German currency

indicators.note: beginning of takes the first letter of pandemic

explanation.surface: The end of May sees the start of a pandemic with the strangest indicator of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns MOST into STOM; 'in' places Y, M and P after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A feature showing that an illness is present is called this, an indication of sickness.

clue.text: It helps in playing a game to be fatuous

indicators.note: the answer is helped into the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Something that helps you play a game makes you look silly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'playinG A GAme'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means foolish or senile, so silly in the way a fatuous remark is.

clue.text: Colourful lie? Young man's worker

parts.note: a flam is an old word for a lie or deception
a boy is a young man
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A lie told about a young man's employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and bright in manner or appearance, so vivid in the way a colourful character is.

clue.text: Connect Internet Relay Chat supply with a common centre

indicators.note: read as an adverb, supply means in a supple way, so the letters are bent into a new shape

parts.note: IRC is the abbreviation for Internet Relay Chat

explanation.surface: Instructions to link an online chat service to the supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not the noun but 'in a supple way', rearranging CONNECT plus IRC.
explanation.definitionFit: Circles drawn one inside another around the same midpoint are described this way, sharing a middle.

clue.text: Fairy king died. Queen starts to oversee nation

parts.note: OB is short for obiit, Latin for he or she died
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: News that a king has died and the queen is beginning to oversee the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream he rules the fairies, married to Titania.

clue.text: Tootling about runs slap into traffic jams

indicators.note: tootling about is wandering aimlessly, so the letters of the two words wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A dawdling driver runs straight into a traffic hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tootling about' mixes up the letters of RUNS SLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal term for knots or tangles in the flow of traffic, so road hold-ups.

clue.text: Have another stab at confining soldiers in records office

indicators.note: confining means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to retry is to have another go
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Trying again to keep soldiers shut up inside the records office.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where official documents such as births and marriages are kept and recorded.

clue.text: Essentially gaffer starts to correct the journalist and put on airs and graces

definitions.note: read as an adjective: having put on airs, pretentious

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so take the middle letters of gaffer
starts to picks the first letters of the two words after it

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's journalist

explanation.surface: The boss begins correcting the reporter, who has become pompous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' strips the outer letters of GAFFER to leave AFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone showy and artificial in manner is described this way, having assumed a false refinement.

clue.text: Short sailor runs up to mast's extremity

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written

indicators.note: the extremity of the mast is its end letter

explanation.surface: A short sailor runs up to the very top of the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt or brusque in manner, as in a terse reply, or sudden and brief.

clue.text: Crazy nut's regret is false

indicators.note: crazy means mixed up, so the letters of nut are scrambled

parts.note: the word nut supplies its own three letters; the possessive adds nothing
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A mad person's remorse is not genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges NUT to UNT; the possessive adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct synonym: not true, so incorrect or deceitful.

clue.text: Established and finished without power and force

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letters are taken away

parts.note: perfected means completed, finished off
P is the physics symbol for power
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Something set up and completed, though lacking energy and strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes P and F from PERFECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up a building or institution is to build it, so put up and set in place.

clue.text: Orange minicab's interior sign

indicators.note: the interior of the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Signage inside an orange taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'oranGE MINIcab'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins is one of the twelve zodiac signs, so an example of a star sign.

clue.text: Have another think about Tory supporter

parts.note: re means about or concerning
CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
a sider is one who sides with, a supporter

explanation.surface: Someone thinking again about backing the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: To think again about a decision means to review it once more, perhaps changing it.

clue.text: Australian regularly can be rash

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words can be

explanation.surface: An Aussie can often be impetuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' reads as hasty, but is the noun for a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots and pimples on the skin form an eruption, one kind of skin outbreak.

clue.text: Heroin? In LA it's a mounting thrill to stash a kilo

indicators.note: mounting means climbing, so in a down answer the letters are read upwards
to stash is to hide away, so one piece is tucked inside the other

parts.note: a gas is slang for something thrilling and fun
K is short for kilo

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler in Los Angeles gets an increasing kick from hiding a kilo of heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stash' tucks K into GAS to give GAKS, which 'mounting' turns upwards. 'In LA' hints the word is slang, chiefly American.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for the opiate drug, heard among users.

clue.text: Clown has to run right back after confusion

indicators.note: after places the run, right and back pieces behind the confusion piece

parts.note: pie is a printer's term for jumbled type, so confusion
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word to backwards

explanation.surface: A clown has to run back right after some muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE, printer's muddled type, comes first; 'back' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock French pantomime character with a white face and loose white costume.

clue.text: To blink frantically is a feature of Rorschach test

indicators.note: done frantically, the letters are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: Nervous blinking is part of a psychology test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' rearranges TO BLINK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rorschach test shows patients symmetrical splodges of spilt ink and asks what they see.

clue.text: Poor Syd Green if out of credit is prone to pilfering

indicators.note: the scrambled letters lie outside the credit piece, which sits within them
poor means in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Poor Syd Green, running out of credit, starts stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' signals the anagram, and 'out of' is read as 'outside', wrapping the scrambled letters around the credit word. On tick is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a thief whose hands seem to make things stick to them, so given to stealing.
